stem: A client responds to the nurse as though the nurse were a significant person from the client's past. What is this phenomenon?

options.A: Transference, in which the client redirects feelings from a past relationship toward the current nurse.
options.B: Countertransference, in which the nurse's own feelings or past experiences shape reactions toward the client.
options.C: Regression, in which stress is associated with a return to an earlier level of coping or behavior.
options.D: Sublimation, in which an unacceptable impulse is redirected into a socially acceptable form of expression.

rationale: Transference occurs when the client transfers feelings associated with another relationship onto the current nurse, so A matches the scenario. B reverses the direction and describes countertransference originating with the clinician. C describes regression under stress. D describes sublimation, in which an unacceptable impulse is channeled into a socially acceptable expression.
educational_objective: Identify transference as client-originating feelings from prior relationships directed toward the current nurse and distinguish it from countertransference and defense mechanisms.
